entries.abstract: There is a countable group G such that the Bernoulli shifts of G with bases (L, lambda) and (L', lambda') are isomorphic for all standard probability spaces whose measures are not point masses: there is an equivariant, measure-preserving bijection, measurable in both directions, between shift-invariant measurable sets of full measure. No condition is put on the entropies of the bases, which may differ and may be infinite. The group is N x (Z/2 wr Z), where N is the group of the pinned OpenAI construction, which supplies the algebraic existence input. This formalization does not certify finitary or continuous conjugacy and says nothing about other groups.
entries.title: A countable group all of whose nontrivial Bernoulli shifts are isomorphic

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. An additive map phi between associative rings is a Jordan homomorphism when phi(ab + ba) = phi(a)phi(b) + phi(b)phi(a). (1) A Jordan homomorphism onto a prime ring without 2-torsion is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism (phi(ab) = phi(b)phi(a)): Herstein's theorem (1956, Theorem H) in the form Smiley gave it (1957, p. 428), with characteristic 3 admitted; an additive map of rings, no identity assumed. (2) The domain form in every characteristic (Jacobson and Rickart 1950, Theorem 2): an additive map with phi(a^2) = phi(a)^2 and phi(aba) = phi(a)phi(b)phi(a), into a ring without zero divisors, is multiplicative or anti-multiplicative, with no surjectivity and no hypothesis on 2. (3)-(5) Each hypothesis of (1) is needed; each statement asserts that one hypothesis fails, that the others hold, and that the map is neither multiplicative nor anti-multiplicative: (3) from 2x2 into 4x4 integer matrices, not onto, the target prime and without 2-torsion (witness a -> diag(a, a^T)); (4) on pairs of 2x2 integer matrices, onto, the target not prime (witness (a, b) -> (a, b^T)); (5) from F_2 x F_2 onto F_2, a prime ring with 2-torsion (witness (x, y) -> x + y). (6) The theorem in every characteristic (Smiley 1957, Added in proof, p. 429): an additive map with the two identities of (2), onto a prime ring, is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism, with no hypothesis on 2; it implies (1), and (5) shows that the Jordan identity alone does not suffice when the ring has 2-torsion. The compared statements add no definition: the identities on the map and the conditions on the target ring are written out as universally quantified statements, the maps are Mathlib's AddMonoidHom, and onto is Function.Surjective. Statements 1, 2 and 6 formalize theorems of the 1950s and statements 3-5 are standard examples; nothing here is a new theorem. The proof of (1) follows the argument written out by Beidar, Bresar and Chebotar (2003, Proposition 3.1), not Smiley's; the proof of (2) is Jacobson and Rickart's; the proof of (6) is Smiley's, through his lemma that a prime ring in which every commutator squares to zero is commutative. Not formalized: the semiprime generalizations. A prior formalization of the case of complex-linear maps between unital complex algebras exists in github.com/openai/math and is recorded under related_formalizations; statements (1) and (6) contain that case. Application (cited; no compared statement asserts it): the self-adjoint elements of an algebra of observables are closed under the symmetrized product and not, in general, under the product; applied to the identity map, (1) says that on a prime ring without 2-torsion the symmetrized product determines the associative product up to reversing the order of the factors.
entries.title: Herstein's theorem on Jordan homomorphisms onto prime rings, in Smiley's form for characteristic different from 2 and in his form for every characteristic, with the Jacobson-Rickart domain theorem and an example for each hypothesis

entries.abstract: For a metric continuum X, D(X) is the hyperspace of subcontinua of X that are the closure of their interior, with the Hausdorff metric. The project formalizes the theorem that a countable D(X) is a G-delta subset of the hyperspace of subcontinua, hence completely metrizable and scattered with dense isolated points, so that D(X) is never homeomorphic to the rationals; together with the structure theory behind it (independent families, blister theorem, complement lemma, absorption by minimal elements, decreasing intersections, density of minimal elements, D-atomic continua, the cardinality dichotomy).
entries.title: On the structure of countable hyperspaces of regular subcontinua

entries.abstract: Formal Lean 4 fixed-quarter Brun–Titchmarsh-type estimate for nonnegative multiplicative weights without squarefree support, with a separate fixed B*n^(1/1280) growth witness. Includes the ordinary modulus-one short-interval corollary with a factor of nine in the bound, and a uniform upper-right parameter-quadrant consequence 1/4 <= alpha,beta < 1/2.
entries.title: Shiu Bounds Toolkit

entries.abstract: Explicit one-tape, two-symbol Turing machines with a designated beep state (Aaronson's beeping busy beaver convention), given as literal transition tables, together with core-Lean proofs (no Mathlib) that each machine, run from the blank tape, beeps only finitely often exactly when a stated Sigma_2 sentence holds. The flagship machine (278 states) is equivalent to the Sigma_2 form of P = NP: some candidate program decides a fixed self-padded NP-complete language within a polynomial clock on every instance. The equivalence of that sentence with P = NP is also proved in Lean (ZP.Cx.sentence_iff_PeqNP) for the Turing-machine models defined in the development. The same guest interpreter yields machines for further Sigma_2 statements (P = PP and P = PSPACE, factoring, discrete logarithm, graph isomorphism, an NTT-based variant over least primes 1 + n i, multiplication, and a co-NP verifier variant), and a 19-state machine that quasihalts iff there are finitely many twin primes.
entries.title: A beeping busy beaver machine for the Σ₂ form of P vs NP

entries.abstract: A general theorem and its six instances. The theorem (congr_of): let k = 12 + 4a + 6b; if the space M_{k−12} of level-one modular forms has rank one and 2k/B_k = D/ℓ with ℓ and D coprime integers, then the q-expansion coefficients of Δ·E₄^a·E₆^b are integers congruent to σ_{k−1}(n) modulo ℓ, for every n. The hypothesis holds exactly for k = 12, 16, 18, 20, 22, 26, where the cusp space is spanned by this one form, and the instances are the congruences modulo the numerator of B_k/2k: 691, 3617, 43867, 174611 = 283·617, 77683 = 131·593 and 657931. The case k = 12 is Ramanujan's τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) (mod 691); the other five are the remaining congruences of this kind at level one. The statements are for every n and use only Mathlib definitions; the Bernoulli numbers B_12 to B_26 are computed in Lean, not assumed. Integrality comes from the product formula for Δ, expanded by Mathlib's pentagonal number theorem, and the integer coefficients 240σ₃ and −504σ₅ of E₄ and E₆. The congruence comes from one exact identity in M_k: E₄^(a+3)·E₆^b − E_k vanishes at the cusp, so dividing by Δ (Mathlib's discriminantEquiv) gives a form in M_{k−12}, which is one-dimensional and spanned by E₄^a·E₆^b; hence E₄^(a+3)·E₆^b − E_k = c·Δ·E₄^a·E₆^b, with c read off from the q¹-coefficient. Since E_k = 1 − (2k/B_k)∑σ_{k−1}(n)qⁿ, multiplying by the numerator of B_k/2k and reducing shows that the Eisenstein series is congruent to the cusp form. The argument is proved once for general (a, b) and applied to the six cases.
entries.title: Ramanujan's congruences for the one-dimensional cusp spaces

entries.abstract: For a nonempty finite set of integers excluding 0, 1, and −1, consider the primes for which every integer in the set is a primitive root. When neither Matthews obstruction occurs, the simultaneous primitive primes have a lower bound of order x/log x in every sufficiently large real dyadic interval (x, 2x] and positive lower relative density among the primes. When either obstruction occurs, the simultaneous primitive primes form a finite set. This is Theorem 1.1 of the accompanying paper.
entries.title: An Unconditional Artin–Matthews Theorem for Simultaneous Primitive Roots

entries.abstract: This submission strengthens PALOMAR-2026-11-09-000019 and is proposed as the next version of that existing registration, using the same repository and Comparator configuration path. Version 1 states that no proper principal upper cone of the ordinary Turing degrees is order-isomorphic to the whole degree structure. This revision proves that two principal upper cones are order-isomorphic if and only if their base degrees are equal, and that every such isomorphism fixes every underlying degree. Consequently, every individual cone has only the identity automorphism. Both compared statements concern arbitrary order isomorphisms, without regularity, determinacy, persistence, or model-existence hypotheses. The earlier theorem remains valid as a special case; this is a substantive strengthening, not a correction or retraction of version 1, whose record and archived source remain unchanged.
entries.title: Pairwise rigidity of principal upper cones of Turing degrees

entries.abstract: A Lean proof that f(n, k), the least number such that the edges of every graph with n vertices and k edges can be partitioned into at most f(n, k) cliques, satisfies f(n, k) = n² B(k/n²) + o(n²) uniformly in 0 ≤ k ≤ n(n − 1)/2, for an explicit continuous piecewise-algebraic function B on [0, 1/2]. B(d) = d for d ≤ 1/4; above 1/4 it is the larger of two curves built from explicit dual certificates on split, mixed and two-head graphs. This provides an asymptotic resolution of Erdős Problem 1017, as posed by Erdős and as stated by Bloom, who asks for an estimate of f(n, k) for k > n²/4. The formula is new to our knowledge. The proof passes through the fractional relaxation and proves again, in Lean, the case of the fractional-to-integral transfer of Balogh, He, Krueger, Nguyen and Wigal that it needs.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 1017: clique partitions of graphs of given size

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.
entries.title: Stafford 3.8

entries.abstract: For every natural N there is n at least N and an n-point set in the single fixed Euclidean space R^29 whose distances on different unordered pairs of distinct points differ by at least one, with diameter strictly below (499/500)n^2. The sizes n form an unbounded set; no claim is made for every large n. As a consequence the formalization proves the negation of the fixed-dimension proposition for Erdős Problem 670 exactly as stated in Formal Conjectures at commit 2f91d251c07fbbaf9435166d47c11e884a08a6cf, using d = 29 and epsilon = 1/1000. No optimality, smallest dimension or independent priority review is claimed.
entries.title: Separated distances in the fixed space R^29

entries.abstract: Let f(y) be the decimal reversal of the y-th prime (f(1) = 2, f(2) = 3, f(5) = 11, f(11) = 13). OEIS A100475 is the orbit of 1 under f, and its entry asks (Jonathan Vos Post, 2004) whether the orbit of any other positive start ever enters a loop. This project proves that it never does, i.e. the negation of the formal-conjectures statement OeisA100475.conjecture: the number of digits never decreases along an orbit (p_y > y, and a prime never ends in 0), so on a cycle it is a constant D and every cycle element v satisfies p_v < 10^D; for D <= 4 this forces v <= 1229, and a kernel-checked table of the first 1230 primes with an escape-time ranking shows that no cycle stays below 1230; for D >= 5 it contradicts the bound pi'(10^D) < 10^(D-1) on the number of primes below 10^D, proved for D = 5, ..., 8 by Legendre's sieve recursion evaluated by the Lean kernel and for D >= 9 by Chebyshev's bound theta(x) <= x log 4 with the split point 10^(D-2).
entries.title: OEIS A100475: the reverse-prime map never loops

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation of Theorems A–F for absorbing Markov chains on compact metric spaces under Hypothesis H. The results give conditional Poisson point-process and shrinking-target limits, stable laws and their Gaussian boundary, an L2 central limit theorem, exponential concentration, and conditional laws of large numbers. The registry statement exposes the canonical path laws, local admissibility, and normalised spectral data; existence of the spectral data is proved from H.
entries.title: Conditional stable laws and rare-event limits for absorbing Markov chains

entries.abstract: For every n >= 4 the Cayley graph of S_n with unit-cost generators L = (0 1 ... n-1), R = L inverse, and X = (0 1) has diameter n*(n-1)/2. The formalization proves upper and lower bounds and a literal L/R/X word of at most that length between every ordered pair of permutations. The independent Challenge defines the moves, their word evaluation, and the undirected Cayley graph using Mathlib alone.
entries.title: Exact LRX diameter of the symmetric group

entries.abstract: A fully-dynamic Maximum-Cardinality-Search (MCS) ordering algorithm that, on a single-edge insertion or deletion into a loop-free undirected graph, scans the affected window between the two endpoints for the first step at which the current ordering's choice stops being a legal MCS pick, and only then regreedies the suffix (probe-then-repair). Correctness - every order produced stays a valid MCS ordering of the updated graph, and in fact equals the from-scratch canonical ordering - is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib, together with locality (the first position whose choice can change lies inside the window between the endpoints; after a break the suffix is regreedyed, so positions past the window may also change), an executable boolean-adjacency implementation proved to refine the abstract update, and per-update cost in a unit-cost query model (counting legality checks and pick steps along the real executable control flow): at most n units for an insertion and n + 1 for a deletion, so the worst case matches static recomputation. A stability theorem is also proved: if the neighbour count of every unchosen vertex in one graph exceeds that in the other by at most one along every *proper common MCS prefix* (the sets the constructive proof actually visits -- a hypothesis strictly weaker than the every-subset bound, which is equivalent to adding a matching), the two graphs admit a common MCS ordering; in particular inserting or deleting a matching, or flipping a single edge, always preserves a common MCS ordering. This strengthening (exists_common_ordering_prefix) makes the matching result a genuine corollary; the every-subset version exists_common_ordering is retained as a special case.
entries.title: Dynamic MCS Ordering Maintenance

entries.abstract: For 1/2 ≤ θ < 1, the Riemann zeta function has no zeros with real part greater than θ if and only if Chebyshev's ψ(x) = x + O(x^{θ+δ}) for every δ > 0. Consequences: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to ψ(x) = x + O(x^{1/2+δ}) for all δ > 0, and the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 (proved by OpenAI in 2026, used here as an explicitly stated hypothesis) yields ψ(x) = x + O(x^{7/8+δ}). Both directions are proved: the easy direction by partial summation and holomorphy of a Mellin transform; the hard direction by a smoothed Chebyshev function, a contour shift to a vertical line inside the zero-free half-plane, and a bound ζ'/ζ(σ+it) ≪ log|t| obtained from the Borel–Carathéodory theorem.
entries.title: Ingham's theorem: zero-free half-planes of the Riemann zeta function and the error term in the prime number theorem

entries.abstract: Let M be the n x n matrix with entries 1/lcm(i,j). R. G. Wilson v conjectured (OEIS A060841, 2015) that 1/det(M) is an integer only for n = 1, ..., 34, 36 and 38. This project proves the conjecture as stated in formal-conjectures (OeisA60841.conjecture1): by Smith's determinant the gcd matrix factors as E diag(phi) E^T with E the unitriangular divisibility matrix, so 1/det(M) = (n!)^2 / prod_{k <= n} phi(k); for n in {1, ..., 34, 36, 38} the divisibility is decided by computation, and for every other n the odd primes up to 97 and the powers of 2 from 4 to 128 force v_2(prod phi(k)) > v_2((n!)^2), numerically for n = 35, 37 and 39 <= n < 100 and by a linear bound for n >= 100.
entries.title: OEIS A060841: 1/det(1/lcm(i,j)) is an integer exactly for n <= 34, n = 36 and n = 38

entries.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Ideal Generation for General Reduced Projective Points. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, for every projective dimension n >= 1, degree D >= 2 and point count between binomial(n+D-1,D-1) and binomial(n+D,D)-1, a nonempty principal open of ordered reduced point configurations has maximal-rank multiplication from I_D tensor S_1 to I_(D+1). The homogeneous ideal has the exact predicted numbers of minimal generators in degrees D and D+1 and is generated in those degrees. Generality is expressed in the standard affine chart of projective space. The points are actual projective classes and their homogeneous ideal is radical.
entries.title: Ideal generation for general reduced projective points

entries.abstract: A general Carleson theorem for doubling measure metric spaces, implying Carleson's classical theorem about pointwise a.e. convergence of Fourier series for continuous periodic functions on the real line
entries.title: Carleson

entries.abstract: For a metric continuum X, a subcontinuum is regular if it equals the closure of its interior, and D(X) denotes the hyperspace of regular subcontinua with the Hausdorff metric. Camargo, Ordoñez and Ramírez asked whether D(X) can be homeomorphic to the rationals or to the irrationals. This project formalizes in Lean 4 with Mathlib the complete proof of the affirmative answer for the irrationals: there is a nondegenerate compact connected set X in the Hilbert space ℓ² such that D(X) is homeomorphic to the Baire space ℕ^ℕ and to the space of irrational numbers. The continuum X is the closure of a countable tree of scaled copies of the Knaster continuum, realized in ℓ² as the inverse limit of the tent map. The formalization proves that the regular subcontinua of X are coded exactly by the nonempty, convex sets of pieces that satisfy a density condition. It shows that this coding is a homeomorphism onto a nonempty, zero-dimensional G_δ subset of a Cantor cube in which every compact set has empty interior. It then concludes with the Alexandrov–Urysohn characterization of the Baire space and the homeomorphism between ℕ^ℕ and the irrationals. Both classical results are also proved in the project.
entries.title: A continuum whose hyperspace of regular subcontinua is homeomorphic to the irrationals

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the theorem that every Lebesgue measurable subset of the plane with positive upper Banach density contains a translated and rotated copy of every sufficiently large dilate of any fixed noncollinear triangle. The proof was developed using GPT 6 Astra Pro. The Lean formalization was generated by Claude Opus 5.5 Medium.
entries.title: Triangles in sets of positive upper density in the plane

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of three existence theorems for discounted stationary first-order mean-field games in positive dimension. Under the paper's monotonicity and respective growth hypotheses, the results give strong solutions for standard power growth and singular congestion, and weak solutions for weak growth. Each result includes density integrability, Sobolev regularity, nonnegativity, identification of the returned weak gradient, and its integrability. The congestion result permits infinite Hamiltonian limits at zero mass and a general continuous limiting flux; the weak-growth result imposes no boundary condition on the original Hamiltonian. The independent Challenge contains the definitions and statements; Solution connects them to the included proof development.
entries.title: Existence of stationary mean-field games by monotonicity methods

entries.abstract: Let N >= 2 be an integer, let u_1 < u_2 < ... be positive integers with liminf u_{j+1}/u_j >= 2, and let lambda_j be nonzero rational numbers with log H(lambda_j) = o(u_j), where H(a/b) = max(|a|, b) in lowest terms. The series x = sum_j lambda_j N^{-u_j} converges absolutely, is irrational, and has irrationality exponent limsup u_{j+1}/u_j, finite or infinite. The coefficients may have arbitrary signs, and the boundary case liminf u_{j+1}/u_j = 2 is included, with ratios allowed to approach 2 from below. The proof compares continued-fraction denominator gaps of consecutive truncations. A perturbation lemma places each new gap in at least one of five classes: bounded, inherited, central, short, or reflected. The reflected class gives the estimate needed at the boundary ratio 2. This project formalizes the paper's main theorem in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
entries.title: The irrationality exponent of small-height lacunary series

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Brouwer's fixed-point theorem in every finite dimension: a continuous map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space into itself has a fixed point. Also proved: the same for closed balls of a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and the no-retraction theorem, that the unit sphere of such a space is not a retract of its closed unit ball.

The proof is analytic, along the lines of Milnor (1978) and Rogers (1980), and uses no homology, degree theory or simplicial approximation. A C1 retraction r of the closed unit ball onto its sphere is ruled out with the change of variables formula: for small t > 0 the map x + t(r(x) - x) sends the open ball bijectively onto itself with positive Jacobian determinant, so the integral of that determinant over the ball, a polynomial in t, equals the volume of the ball for every t, whereas at t = 1 it vanishes. Brouwer's theorem follows for C1 self-maps of the ball by the ray construction, for continuous ones by smoothing by convolution, and for compact convex sets through the nearest-point retraction. Brouwer's theorem has earlier formal proofs in HOL Light, Isabelle/HOL and Mizar, in Coq for the plane, in Lean 3 through singular homology, and in Lean 4 for the plane and for the standard simplex; this proof is independent of them. A second proof follows Knaster, Kuratowski and Mazurkiewicz (1929): Sperner's lemma for the iterated barycentric subdivisions of the simplex, by counting facets mod 2, then the KKM lemma and Brouwer's theorem for the simplex; Kakutani's and Schauder's proofs use this one, the proof of Brouwer's theorem that both papers cite.

Kakutani's fixed-point theorem (1941) and Schauder's fixed-point theorem (1930) are derived from Brouwer's. Kakutani's: a set-valued map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space, with closed graph and nonempty convex values, has a point x in its own value at x; it is proved by Kakutani's argument (piecewise-linear approximations on barycentric subdivisions of a simplex, Brouwer, a limit along a subsequence, then a retraction for general compact convex sets), and a second time through a partition of unity. Schauder's: a continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a real normed space of any dimension has a fixed point, and so does a continuous self-map of a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Banach space with relatively compact image; it is proved by Schauder's argument, a simplicial approximation on a fine triangulation of the convex hull of a finite epsilon-net and Brouwer's theorem, then compactness, with Mazur's theorem for the second form, and a second time through Schauder's projection.
entries.title: The fixed-point theorems of Brouwer, Kakutani and Schauder, with an analytic proof of Brouwer's theorem and one through Sperner's lemma

entries.abstract: Formalizes the target lowMul3, the three low bits of the product of two 3-bit integers (the product modulo 8), in the unrestricted XOR--AND circuit model of arXiv:2608.30238v1, where XOR and constants are free and either input of a paid AND gate may reuse arbitrary earlier nonlinear wires. Phase 1 proves that the three ANF coordinates agree with integer multiplication modulo 8 on all 64 inputs, and gives an explicit six-gate circuit, one of whose gates reuses two earlier nonlinear wires. Phase 2 adds the derivative lemma (Lemma 8 of the four-gate note in paper/notes/). Phase 3 proves the normal form (Lemma 1), Lemma 2, the pi2 / iota layer with Lemma 8 in the paper's form, Lemma 4 (kernel) and Lemma 6, excludes lambda = 5, and reduces MC(lowMul3) = 6 to four explicit statements. Phase 4 proves the four-linear-gate case (StarFree, Theorem 12 of the note). Phases 5 and 6 prove the three-linear-gate case (lambdaCase_three), so MC(lowMul3) = 6 follows from LambdaCase 1 and LambdaCase 2. The development proves both remaining cases, including TwoClaim and the shared modular feedback lemmas. LowHalfMul3Solution.lean proves the unconditional theorem mc_lowMul3.
entries.title: Unrestricted Boolean multiplicative complexity of the 3x3 low-half multiplier

entries.abstract: We prove concentration of the realized table of matches in balanced tiered random matching markets under men-proposing deferred acceptance. With fixed finite tier counts, positive population shares a_i and b_j, and fixed positive public scores, every participant independently draws a complete ranking by weighted sampling without replacement. The fraction of all couples joining women's tier i to men's tier j converges in probability to a_i b_j. The theorem allows arbitrary tier-label sequences whose counts differ from n times their prescribed shares by at most one. It proves the exact statement of Formal Conjectures PR 7841, corresponding to Remark H.1 in Tiered Random Matching Markets (2021). The development proves the exponential-arrival representation of the exact profile law, the fixed-woman proposal estimate needed from Proposition G.2 with rounding uniformity, and the independent reference coupling used for concentration.
entries.title: Concentration of match types in tiered random matching markets

entries.abstract: Erdős Problem 881 asks whether every minimal additive basis A of order k (one from which no infinite set can be removed while keeping a basis of order k) contains an infinite set B such that A \ B is a basis of order k + 1. This formalization settles the case k = 2 in the formulation of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, where a basis of order n is an asymptotic basis: all but finitely many natural numbers are sums of exactly n elements of A. It proves the stronger statement that every asymptotic additive basis of order 2 in the natural numbers, minimal or not, contains an infinite set whose removal leaves an asymptotic additive basis of order 3. The proof splits on whether some positive difference occurs infinitely often in A. If one does, a sparse set of elements in one residue class, each of whose removal is compensated through two fixed shifts, can be deleted together. If none does, elements are deleted one at a time while the representations already used are protected, and a combinatorial argument shows that this process never gets stuck. As a corollary it answers a question of Erdős and Nathanson (1980): a minimal asymptotic basis of order 3 cannot be an asymptotic basis of order 2. The cases k >= 3 of Problem 881 remain open.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 881 for k = 2: infinite deletions from asymptotic bases of order two

entries.abstract: Actual finite assignment pool, exact-minimum choice, complete connectivity checker, genuine disconnected-fiber boundary cuts, strict progress and history preservation yield terminal optimum or cap-relative infeasibility; cap n covers every finite fiber. All existing owning control propositions are complete compared SUPPORT components.
entries.title: Complete finite connectivity checker and exact cut procedure

entries.abstract: The actual mixed-history recursion has its own master/state/reachability and accepts every exact selector and valid finite pool. Initialization has three branches: an empty relaxation certifies original infeasibility; an admitted integral relaxation minimizer returns a direct exact original minimum without stored-event provenance or loop decisions; fractional initialization runs the mixed loop, yielding certified infeasibility or a stored original-feasible epsilon-optimum with retained decorated-event provenance, exact at epsilon zero. The bound activeY.card+1<=integers.card+1 concerns main loop decisions in the loop branch, not all pooled fixed solves or initialization.
entries.title: Initialized mixed PSC and quadratic OA finite stored return

entries.abstract: Complete generic initialized unseeded execution and finite return with explicit empty/attained continuous initialization, restoration-only prefixes, first feasible handoff, fixed original master anchor, stored current incumbent, fresh integer targets and exact empty/epsilon-correct outcomes. Full named initialized and total seven-ranking return retaining each actual statewise minimum certificate, convex physical objective, current-incumbent ranking centre, fixed initialization/master anchor, distinct history and initializer/event/master inspection counts.
entries.title: Initialized unseeded seven-ranking finite return and empty outcomes

entries.abstract: Full concrete two-stage execution retaining the actual pump seed, incumbent, histories, successful no-goods and strictly pre-last-success normals, then corrected hard OA without reinitialization. Derived choices and exact combined counts accompany certified infeasibility or epsilon-optimal original feasibility.
entries.title: Actual warm pump-to-hard-OA composition

entries.abstract: A finite-graph formalization of nonlinear and linear QUBO penalties for the maximum k-colorable vertex-subset problem. It retains the earlier nonlinear interface and adds jointly optimized binary slack arrays, exact sequential feasibility repair, strict versus weak penalty guarantees, one-color exceptions and universal value thresholds. An unchanged companion follows the manuscript’s strict nonlinear single-slot-deletion proof.
entries.title: Finite MkCS exact penalties, universal thresholds and sequential repair

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of dimension formulas for planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations and their equilibrium measures. The headline results are Theorems A, B and 4.16; Solution.lean presents the numbered statements in manuscript order.
entries.title: Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations: Lean formalisation

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper's main theorem: for any permutations π and σ of the d and e intervals, the set of pairs of length vectors (λ, μ) for which the two interval exchange transformations f_{π,λ} and f_{σ,μ} generate a free group of rank 2 has measure zero. The development contains the irreducible case (Theorem 2.6, from unique ergodicity, rigidity by translations and the Diophantine condition), the almost-everywhere Diophantine property (Proposition 2.5, from the easy direction of Khintchine–Groshev), Lemma 3.1 (the length map of the composition is injective and absolutely continuous), the reduction of the general case to the blocks between consecutive pair-splitting singularities (Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3), Lemma 3.4 (a word trivial on a block, obtained by rescaling the block and applying Theorem 2.6 to it), and the assembly of the per-block words into a single nontrivial word. Masur–Veech unique ergodicity and Veech's rigidity are proved as well, by the Rauzy–Veech induction (`IETFree/RauzyVeech/`, `IETFree/Rigidity/`, `IETFree/UniqueErgodicity/`), so the main theorem is unconditional. The remark that follows the main theorem — the relation of a trivial word is robust, so the pairs that do not generate a free group contain an open set of full measure — is proved in `IETFree/Pair/RobustRelation/`: the symbolic data of an arbitrary word and the robustness at a point of the conull set `Ω'` (`evalWord_eventually_eq_one`), and the assembly of the open conull set (`exists_isOpen_subset_hasRelation_of_ae`), which `ChallengeSolved.lean` feeds with the a.e. relation it proves from `main` — the conclusion on `Δ_π × Δ_σ` is `exists_isOpen_ae_exists_nontrivial_evalWordEquiv_eq_one`.
entries.title: IETFree — almost every pair of interval exchange transformations does not generate a free group

entries.abstract: Lean verification of the inequality in Theorem 1: the word-length log-Sobolev inequality on ZMod n for n ≥ 4 and nonnegative real functions.
entries.title: Log-Sobolev inequality on finite cyclic groups

entries.abstract:
The Reinhardt problem asks for the centrally symmetric convex disk in the plane whose densest packing by congruent copies is least dense. Karl Reinhardt (1934) and, independently, Kurt Mahler (1947) found the smoothed octagon, a regular octagon whose corners are cut off by arcs of hyperbolas, each asymptotic to the next two side lines, with greatest packing density delta_oct = (8 - 4 sqrt 2 - log 2)/(2 sqrt 2 - 1) = 0.902414..., and Reinhardt conjectured that no centrally symmetric convex disk packs worse. The conjecture has been open since 1934; Thomas Hales cast it as a problem of Bolza in the calculus of variations (2011) and then as an optimal control problem on SL2(R) (2017), and Hales and Koundinya Vajjha studied that problem in Packings of Smoothed Polygons (2024).

This entry proves the conjecture with its equality case. Every centrally symmetric convex disk has greatest packing density at least delta_oct, with equality if and only if the disk is the image of the smoothed octagon under an invertible affine map; and the smoothed octagon, in Reinhardt's description, is a centrally symmetric convex disk of greatest packing density delta_oct.

The proof follows Hales's control formulation. A worst disk is realized by a global minimizer of the control problem, which lifts to a Pontryagin extremal, stays in Hales and Vajjha's compact domain, switches finitely often and is normal. Its switch signs fall into five classes, each excluded for periods with at least six pieces by scalar estimates; periods with at most five pieces cost at least the octagon's area, with equality only for the octagon. The scalar estimates are inequalities, polynomial identities, monotonicity and convexity arguments; a few polynomial signs are checked by explicit Bernstein expansions, and no interval cover is used. The geometric and control-theoretic foundations, among them Fejes Toth's lattice theorem, Theorem 5.0.2 of Hales and Vajjha and the Pontryagin maximum principle, come from the pinned libraries lean4-smoothed-polygon and lean4-optimal-control.
entries.title: The Reinhardt conjecture, formalized in Lean 4

entries.abstract: We prove the Lennon–Pittel conjecture for balanced stable marriage with independent, uniform strict preferences. Let S_n count the stable complete matchings between two sides of size n. For every positive nonincreasing sequence epsilon_n tending to zero, the probability that S_n is at least epsilon_n times its expectation tends to one. This gives a lower-tail estimate at the scale of Pittel's first-moment asymptotic. An accompanying working paper is in preparation.
entries.title: The Lennon–Pittel conjecture on random stable matchings

entries.abstract: Switching costs relax pairwise stability by requiring both members of a blocking pair to gain more than a common nonnegative cost. In balanced markets with n firms and n workers and independent rate-one exponential utilities, this package proves a conditional benchmark for ordinal partner ranks in Lean. Fix a matching and condition the market on its stability. If twice the cost divided by log n tends to rho in [0,1), the conditional probability that average one-based firm partner rank is at most n^t tends to (t-rho)/(1-rho) for every rho<t<1; rank 1 is best. Equivalently, the logarithm of average firm rank divided by log n converges in distribution to the uniform law on [rho,1]. Bounded or vanishing costs give rho=0, with persistent dispersion across polynomial rank scales under this conditioning. The theorem removes the original conjecture's supercritical lower bound. The proof also includes positive conditioning probability, exact integral identities, score limits, and rank-transfer estimates. This fixed-matching conditioning does not determine ranks under a uniform stable lottery in an ordinary random market, or dispersion of stable outcomes within a typical realized market. An accompanying working paper presenting these results and their economic interpretation is in preparation. A link will be added here when it is publicly available.
entries.title: Conditional logarithmic partner ranks in exponential matching markets

entries.abstract: We formalize in Lean the principal statistical and constrained-landscape results of Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA by Jagannath, Lopatto and Miolane, following a local expanded manuscript prepared solely by Patrick Lopatto, the formalization’s maintainer. This elaborated manuscript was prepared to facilitate autoformalization. At nonnegative signal strength in the ordered Gaussian tensor model, we prove the detection threshold below and above criticality for even orders k ≥ 6. For k ≥ 3, we prove the maximum-likelihood value limit at every nonnegative signal strength and the maximum-likelihood absolute-overlap limit away from criticality. We prove optimality bounds for independently randomized measurable unit estimators at nonnegative noncritical strengths, and tensor MMSE formulas at positive noncritical strengths. We also prove the discontinuous overlap transition, consistent testing among fixed nonempty finite families of distinct supercritical strengths, constrained expected and almost-sure energy limits for signed overlaps in [-1,1], and associated variational and landscape conclusions. Almost-sure limits concern fixed parameters and allow arbitrary coupling across dimensions. For interior overlaps, the four-parameter variational reduction establishes equality of infima; unrestricted minimizer attainment is not claimed.
entries.title: Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA

entries.abstract: In any finite abelian group G, fix a three-element support S and retain the entire labelled ordered additive convolution square, including diagonal pairs. The number of three-element supports with the same square is h or 2h, where h is the number of elements u satisfying u+u=0; in particular it is at most 2h. The full proof is included. This adapts a prior public Couret formalization; novelty and independent human review are not established.
entries.title: Cardinalities of three-point ordered convolution-square fibres

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g points of its boundary, which together must see the whole closed polygon (the boundary-point variant), is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. The orthogonal point-point and point-boundary variants are the subject of the author's earlier entry PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000004 v1, whose definitions this entry reuses unchanged. For general polygons the boundary-point variant is treated by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021); orthogonal polygons are not. The hardness proof is a new construction: the ETR-INV instance is compiled to rows of fourteen relation profiles, and the polygon is a hub with one floor slot per variable and one door per row, behind each of which hangs an orthogonal wing (a staircase corridor ending in an arithmetic room) whose boundary guards copy the slot values through the door and enforce the row relation. Its finite visibility facts are kernel-checked certificates on the wing charts, parametric in the size and value parameters. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: The orthogonal boundary-point art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Morse index and nullity of Karcher saddle towers, formalizing results from arXiv:2608.13451v2. For the Enneper-Weierstrass realizations, the two-period quotient Xi_{k,2} has index 4k-3 and bounded Jacobi-field nullity 3 for every k >= 3. For the six-ended family Xi_{3,m}, every positive integer m has index 6m-4 floor(m alpha*)-3 and nullity 7 when m alpha* is an integer, and 3 otherwise. The same threshold alpha* lies in (1/3,1/2), with certified strict bounds 0.4323617 < alpha* < 0.4323619. As in the paper, index and nullity are defined using complex-valued functions, with dimensions taken over the complex numbers. The development constructs realizations from the explicit data and supplies the geometric-to-analytic identifications, rather than assuming the existence of a realization. Supporting results include proper embeddedness and the equivalence of boundedness and finite Dirichlet energy for smooth geometric Jacobi fields on the finite period quotients.
entries.title: KarcherIndex

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof that an infinite set of points in the Euclidean plane whose pairwise distances are all integers is contained in a line (Anning and Erdős, 1945). Formal Conjectures states it next to the Erdős-Ulam problem on dense rational-distance sets, which is open; its audience is distance problems in discrete geometry. It is the statement erdos_ulam_problem.variants.anning_erdos of Formal Conjectures (ErdosUlamProblem.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The proof follows Erdős's short argument: for three points A, B, C not on a line, the differences |PA| - |PB| and |PA| - |PC| take finitely many values, and in place of the bound on how often two hyperbolas meet, each pair of values is shown to allow only finitely many points P, as the roots of a quadratic in |PA|.
entries.title: The Anning-Erdős theorem: an infinite set of points in the plane with integer distances lies on a line

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the exact minimum number of coprime adjacent pairs over all permutations of the first n positive integers, valid unconditionally for every n at least four. The proof constructs optimal paths in the graph joining noncoprime integers.
entries.title: The Minimum Number of Coprime Adjacencies in a Permutation

entries.abstract: For three-element finite supports S and T in any abelian group, equality of all labelled coefficients of their ordered additive convolution squares is equivalent to a translation by an element annihilated by doubling, or to the explicit exceptional paired shape in the statement. Diagonal pairs are included. The full proof development is contained in this snapshot. This is an adaptation of an existing public Couret formalization; mathematical novelty and independent human review are not established.
entries.title: Three-point ordered convolution-square classification

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Fournier's theorem (1973): if the vertices of maximum degree of a finite simple graph G induce a forest, then G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) colours (fournier: G.lineGraph.Colorable G.maxDegree under (G.induce {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}).IsAcyclic). The proof takes an edge-minimal subgraph H of G that is not Δ(G)-edge-colourable; Vizing's theorem gives Δ(H) = Δ(G), and Vizing's adjacency lemma applied to every edge xy of H gives a neighbour of x of maximum degree other than y, so the maximum-degree vertices of H span a subgraph of minimum degree at least 2 inside the forest, which is impossible (the end of a longest path). Vizing's theorem and the adjacency lemma are imported as lake dependencies from PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. One statement; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: Fournier's theorem: graphs whose maximum-degree vertices induce a forest are of class one

entries.abstract: Verification that the König constant is one, as shown in the source.
entries.title: The König constant is one

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Walecki's theorem: for every m, the complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices is the edge-disjoint union of m Hamiltonian cycles (hamiltonian_cycles_odd), and the complete graph on 2m vertices is the edge-disjoint union of m Hamiltonian paths (hamiltonian_paths_even). Both are stated for an arbitrary finite vertex type of the given cardinality, with Mathlib's Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle and Walk.IsHamiltonian, pairwise disjoint edge lists, and every edge of the complete graph on some cycle (path). The proof is Walecki's zig-zag construction: on ZMod (2m) the paths i, i+1, i−1, i+2, i−2, …, i+m (0 ≤ i < m) are Hamiltonian; an edge {x, y} of the i-th path has x + y ∈ {2i, 2i+1}, which makes the paths edge-disjoint, and m (2m − 1) = C(2m, 2) shows that they cover all edges; closing each path through a new vertex gives the cycles. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: Walecki's decompositions of complete graphs into Hamiltonian cycles and paths

entries.abstract: A complete source-based finite penalty/energy family: the generic full ordered QUBO identity and strict integer-row minimizer equivalence, consistent fixed-coordinate energy/minimizer transport, and the literal incidence, time-indexed arc and sequence applications. The statements retain actual rows, repeated costs, full offsets, source free/fixed partitions, feasibility conditions, strict sufficient thresholds and finite source energy attainment. Capacity, physical route completeness and solver/quantum performance are outside scope.
entries.title: Finite integer penalties and literal routing QUBO transport

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of M. Mirek and C. Thiele, "A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators", Proc. London Math. Soc. 114 (2017): the perfect multilinear local T(1) theorem (Theorem 1.3), the perfect multilinear local T(b) theorem with general testing functions on admissible collections of paths (Theorem 1.4), and the perfect multilinear global T(b) theorem (Theorem 1.11), for n-linear forms on dyadic test functions in R^d satisfying the dyadic decay, perfect smoothness and qualitative truncation conditions. The development follows the paper's proof of Theorem 1.4 (stopping times, pruning, the telescoping identities, the discrete Carleson embedding and the outer-measure Hölder inequalities of Do–Thiele, the contraction step and its iteration) and the global/local reduction of Theorem 1.11, including the atom estimate for the dyadic Hardy norm for all exponents (Burkholder's L^p bound for the dyadic square function by Marcinkiewicz interpolation). Theorem 1.3, cited as folklore in the paper, is proved by a dyadic paraproduct argument with a dyadic John–Nirenberg inequality for the paraproduct symbols. All constants depend only on the dimension, the linearity, the testing constant and the exponents.
entries.title: A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators (Mirek–Thiele), formalized in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A thin wrapper that restates, in one vocabulary and with Mathlib definitions only, the overfull criteria proved in PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000016 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. class_two_iff_overfull_subgraph: a finite simple graph of even order n with 12 n ≤ 7 (3δ − Δ) is of class two (its line graph is not Δ-colourable) iff it has a Δ-overfull subgraph (odd order at least 3, more than Δ (|V(H)| − 1)/2 edges); this is Plantholt's criterion with Chetwynd–Hilton's 6/7. critical_overfull: a Δ-critical graph (connected, class two, every edge-deleted subgraph Δ-colourable) with 2n + 5δ ≤ 3Δ + 6 (Chen–Cao), or 3n + 7δ ≤ 4Δ + 10 (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan, variant), or 3n + 7δ ≤ 4Δ + 17 and n + δ ≥ 27 (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan) has odd order, is overfull (|E| > Δ ⌊n/2⌋), and so is a Δ-overfull subgraph of itself. The only new proof is the elementary step from overfullness to odd order at least 3 (degree sum) and the conversion to the subgraph form. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: Overfull criteria for edge colouring (Plantholt; Chen–Cao; Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan), unified

entries.abstract: This project formalizes the main central limit theorem of “Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices” by Advay Goel, Patrick Lopatto, and Xiaoyu Xie (arXiv:2306.10243v2), using an expanded local manuscript as the detailed proof source. The local manuscript was prepared to ease autoformalization by adding details to the proofs. Its main theorem (Theorem 1.3) is identical to the main theorem of the arXiv version: the hypotheses and conclusion are unchanged. Only this main theorem is advertised.
entries.title: Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of two results on sums of four squares. (1) Jacobi's four-square theorem for odd N: the number of x : Fin 4 → ℤ with x₀² + x₁² + x₂² + x₃² = N equals 8 ∑_{d ∣ N} d (jacobi_four_squares_odd), following the proof of Andrews, Ekhad and Zeilberger (1993): two finite q-series identities proved by WZ telescoping, combined into a finite identity that is read modulo X^{N+1} in ℚ⟦X⟧. (2) Four squares in caps (four_squares_in_caps): for every unit vector q ∈ ℝ⁴ and every δ > 0 there is M₀ such that every odd m ≥ M₀ is β₀² + β₁² + β₂² + β₃² with β : Fin 4 → ℤ and |βᵢ − √m qᵢ| ≤ δ √m for all i, i.e. the integer points of the sphere of radius √m meet every cap of fixed angular radius. The proof uses the Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec delta method (in Heath-Brown's form) with Gaussian weights: an exact formula through the theta transformation, Fourier bounds for the cut-off weight, and the Weil bound for Kloosterman sums, imported from the Weil Bounds Toolkit (PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000018) as a lake dependency. The main term is not evaluated: it depends on the center of the cap only through its norm, so comparing caps with a grid of centers reduces the theorem to the lower bound r₄(m) ≥ 8m for odd m, which (1) provides. All constants are effective but not explicit in the statement (M₀ is existential). Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: Four squares in caps, and Jacobi's four-square theorem for odd N

entries.abstract: For every transcendental r > 2, the seven points (0, 0) and (j, ±√(j(2r − j))), j ∈ {1, 3, 4}, lie on the circle of centre (r, 0) and radius r and are not Euclidean Ramsey (Pálvölgyi, A cyclic non-Ramsey heptagon, arXiv:2609.23327, Theorem 1); consequently not every finite cospherical subset of a Euclidean space is Ramsey. The second statement is the negation of the conjecture that every finite spherical set is Ramsey (posed by Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus in 1973), in exactly the form in which google-deepmind/formal-conjectures states it as erdos_174.variants.graham (formal-conjectures PR #7706, which re-tags that statement as solved and links this proof). Ramsey is formal-conjectures' definition, Erdos174.IsRamsey, copied byte for byte: a finite set A in R^n such that for every number k ≥ 1 of colours there is a dimension d for which every k-colouring of R^d has a monochromatic distance-preserving copy of A. All four compared statements use only Mathlib and that definition. The conjecture was refuted in September 2026 by Pálvölgyi's paper (whose proofs it attributes to ChatGPT) and by OpenAI's classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations, whose Lean proof (openai/math) already exhibits non-Ramsey twelve- and nine-point sets on a circle in OpenAI's own vocabulary. The proof here is Pálvölgyi's derivation-energy argument run against OpenAI's tensor criterion: a derivation D of R with D r = 1, the pairing x ⊗ y ↦ D x · D y on OpenAI's coefficient tensor ring, the weights 2, −2, −2, 2, 2, −1, −1 and the energy −24/((2r − 1)(2r − 3)(2r − 4)) ≠ 0 show that the heptagon fails OpenAI's field criterion, and the necessity half of OpenAI's classification (proved in their Lean) turns that into not Ramsey; formal-conjectures' IsRamsey, which also allows the dimension d = 0, is then reduced to OpenAI's Ramsey. The witness for the second statement is the heptagon at r = 2 + OpenAI's Liouville-type parameter, which is transcendental. Also proved, with the same definition: Theorem A.3 of the paper's appendix as printed, without its measure clause (for distinct t1, t2, t3 and t4, ..., t7 algebraically independent over Q(t1, t2, t3), the seven points ((1 − ti²)/(1 + ti²), 2ti/(1 + ti²)) are not Ramsey; the appendix is labelled by its author as written by ChatGPT and unchecked), and its corollary for seven parameters algebraically independent over Q, in the shape of OpenAI's nine-point theorem (distinct points on the unit circle, not Ramsey). Its proof follows the appendix: Lemma A.1 in its symmetric form, a derivation vanishing on Q(t1, t2, t3) with prescribed values on t4, ..., t7, weighted moments by Lagrange interpolation, and again the necessity half of OpenAI's classification. The 16 OpenAI Lean files the proofs import are included, ported to the Lean module system by header-only changes. All proofs depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
entries.title: Pálvölgyi's cyclic heptagon is not Euclidean Ramsey, so Graham's spherical-set conjecture (formal-conjectures erdos_174.variants.graham) is false; and generic seven points on a circle are not Ramsey (Theorem A.3 of arXiv:2609.23327)

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying S. Vorobev, "On the inclusion D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G): reductions, the Lie-ring proof, and evidence" (preprint, 2026; submitted to arXiv math.GR on 2026-10-22). The integral dimension subgroups D_n(G) = {g ∈ G : g − 1 ∈ Δ(G)^n} are defined from the augmentation ideal of Mathlib's integral group ring. Kourovka Problem 20.84 asks whether D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G) for every group; it is open and is not claimed here. Unconditional results: D_5(G) = γ_5(G) whenever G/γ_2(G) is finite of exponent 3, and more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group whose cubes form a cyclic group, and still more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group and γ_2(G)/γ_3(G) has exponent at most 3, and still more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group, γ_4(G)^3 ⊆ γ_5(G) and γ_2(G)^9 ⊆ γ_4(G), and most generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group and γ_4(G)^3 ⊆ γ_5(G) (paper, Theorems 6.6, 6.8, 6.9, 6.10 and 6.11), and whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite p-group, p odd, and [γ_2(G), γ_2(G)] ⊆ γ_5(G), in particular for finite metabelian 3-groups, which is Gupta–Tahara's theorem at p = 3 (paper, Theorem D.1; the inclusion part of Tahara's 1981 description of D_5 is formalized for this); D_5(G) lies in the Jennings product M_5(G) for finite 2-groups of class at most 3; and, for "candidates" (the paper's minimal-counterexample shape among finite 2-groups of class 3), there is no candidate of order 2^11 with Q/P_3 ≅ Z/4 × (Z/2)^7 and none of order 2^11 and rank at least 8 (paper, Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7); the reduction of Problem 20.84 to finite 2-groups of class exactly 3 (Proposition 2.1); and a minimal counterexample is a candidate (Lemma 5.2). The proofs of the last two use D_3 = γ_3, Passi's D_4^2 ⊆ γ_4 and Gruenberg's residual theorem, all proved in the development (dThreeEqGammaThree, passiDFourSquare, gruenbergResidualTwo). One conditional result, with the assumption an explicit hypothesis: D_5 = 1 for groups of order 2^11, class at most 3 and rank at least 8, assuming the paper's computer result for order 2^10 (Proposition 5.7, D_5 form, assuming Proposition 5.3).
entries.title: Fifth dimension subgroups: D₅ = γ₅ when G/γ₂ is finite of exponent 3, candidates for a counterexample, and a reduction of Kourovka 20.84

entries.abstract: A complete classification of the globally periodic rational difference equations x_{n+K} = (A_0 + A_1 x_n + ... + A_K x_{n+K-1}) / (B_0 + B_1 x_n + ... + B_K x_{n+K-1}) with nonnegative coefficients, acting on positive initial data, answering Problem 11 of Gasull's survey of open problems in low-dimensional dynamical systems. Such an equation is globally periodic (every positive solution satisfies x_{n+p} = x_n for a common p >= 1) if and only if, up to rescaling x_n -> alpha x_n and unfolding (multiplying every index by an integer), it is one of the five known examples: x_{n+1} = x_n, x_{n+1} = 1/x_n, x_{n+2} = x_{n+1}/x_n, the Lyness equation x_{n+2} = (1 + x_{n+1})/x_n, and Todd's period-8 equation x_{n+3} = (1 + x_{n+1} + x_{n+2})/x_n. The result holds at every order K. Previously the question had been settled for K in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11} (Cima, Gasull and Mañosas 2004) and for some special families, but the general case was open.
entries.title: Classification of globally periodic rational difference equations

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof that a finite-dimensional real normed space whose linear isometries act transitively on the unit sphere is Euclidean. This is the finite-dimensional case of the Mazur rotations problem, which appeared in Banach's 1932 book and is surveyed by Cabello Sanchez, Ferenczi and Randrianantoanina; its audience is the geometry of Banach spaces and their symmetries. It is the statement banach_mazur_rotation_problem.finite_dimensional of Formal Conjectures (BanachMazurRotation.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The proof takes the classical route: the isometries form a compact group, averaging a squared Euclidean norm over Haar measure gives an invariant quadratic form, and transitivity makes it a multiple of the squared norm. Mathlib has no topology on the isometry group, so the entry also builds it as a compact topological group with Haar measure. The general problem for separable Banach spaces, which Formal Conjectures marks research open, is not addressed.
entries.title: The Banach-Mazur rotation problem in finite dimensions: a transitive isometry group forces a Euclidean norm

entries.abstract: A qualified finite sequence-routing formalization connecting the complete source binary rows with padded elementary customer routes and exact transition cost. For fixed valid slots, explicit zero-depot clock/travel conditions give continuous timing feasibility through the earliest-schedule recurrence and an attained minimum total return over timing assignments. Capacity and global route optimization are outside scope.
entries.title: Finite sequence routing formulations and continuous timing

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the three squares theorem of Legendre (1798) and Gauss (1801): a natural number is a sum of three squares if and only if it is not of the form 4^a (8 b + 7) (sum_three_sq_iff), with the corollary that every n ≡ 3 (mod 8) is x₀² + x₁² + x₂² for some x : Fin 3 → ℤ (exists_sum_sq_of_mod_eight_eq_three). The proof uses ternary quadratic forms of determinant one: a positive definite integral ternary form of determinant one is equivalent to x² + y² + z² (proved with Minkowski's convex body theorem), and for n ≢ 0 (mod 4), n ≢ 7 (mod 8) such a form with diagonal entry n is built from a prime in an arithmetic progression (Dirichlet's theorem, as in Mathlib) and quadratic reciprocity for the Jacobi symbol. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: The three squares theorem (Gauss–Legendre)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib library for Poincare inequalities, log-concave probability measures and stochastic localization. Its dimension-free KLS theorem bounds the intrinsic local-slope Poincare constant by one universal constant times the covariance operator norm, including dimension zero and singular affine supports, for log-concave probability laws with finite second moment. The proof follows Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec through finite-horizon cutoff localization, the compact Letwin constant-8 quadratic variance bound and approximation. Supporting results include Cheeger-Buser comparisons, covariance and energy interfaces and moment-map calculus. This Palomar configuration compares two density statements. Each asserts the existence of a positive constant C that works in every dimension n >= 1 and for every measurable isotropic log-concave probability density. The pinned OpenAI statement gives Var(f) <= C * E|grad f|^2 for smooth compactly supported tests and is the statement registered in PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000014 v1. The density-coordinate formulation of Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec Theorem 1.1 applies to every locally Lipschitz f in L^2 and uses an extended nonnegative squared-gradient integral that may be infinite. The locally Lipschitz definitions and bridge are new project code, not part of the OpenAI model. No numerical final KLS constant or uncut Eldan construction is claimed.
entries.title: Dimension-free KLS Poincare bound for isotropic log-concave densities

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proofs of the main results of Addario-Berry, Donderwinkel and Kortchemski, "Critical trees are neither too short nor too fat" (arXiv:2311.06163). For every critical offspring law, the height of the size-conditioned Bienaymé tree divided by log n tends to infinity and its width divided by n tends to zero in probability, along admissible sizes. These bounds are sharp: for every function f tending to infinity, a single critical offspring law has limsup P(height < f(n) log n) = 1 and limsup P(width > n/f(n)) = 1. For critical offspring laws in the local domain of attraction of the asymmetric Cauchy law (mu_n = L(n)/n^2 with L slowly varying), the height divided by an explicit scale h_n and the width divided by n E[Y 1{Y >= a_n}] both converge to 1 in probability, and height times width is O_P(n log n). The entry also includes the stochastic ordering of heights of uniform labelled trees with given degree sequences (Addario-Berry and Donderwinkel, Theorem 9), used in the paper. All 23 named results of the paper (its theorem, proposition, lemma and corollary environments) are proved in the repository; this Palomar entry compares the headline results.
entries.title: Critical trees are neither too short nor too fat

entries.abstract: A combinatorial arrangement of pseudolines in the real projective plane, given as a generalised map with flags labelled by lines, in which no line carries fewer than three vertices, is four lines in general position or contains five lines in general position, a pencil of three and a pencil of two in which none of these five lines joins the two centres, or the complete quadrangle.
entries.title: Bigon-free dichotomy for combinatorial pseudoline arrangements

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of C. Thomassen, Exponentially many 5-list-colorings of planar graphs (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 97, 2007): a finite planar graph with n vertices, every vertex of which has a list of at least five colours, has at least 2^{n/9} distinct list colourings (two_rpow_card_div_nine_le_ncard_listColourings: (2 : ℝ) ^ (n / 9) ≤ the number of maps f : V → C with f v ∈ L v and f u ≠ f v on every edge). Planarity is combinatorial: a plane map is a rotation system whose hypermap with the dart reversal has Euler defect 0 (definitions copied verbatim from the registered entry thomassen-girth-five, PALOMAR-2026-10-28-000023, so that the Challenge depends on Mathlib only). The proof follows the paper: Theorems 1–4, Claims 8–13 and the lemmas on generalized wheels they use are proved for an abstract interface of near-triangulations, which is realised by plane near-triangulations using the separation theorems of the dependency; every planar graph is a spanning subgraph of a plane near-triangulation. One statement; the definitions of the Challenge are compared with those of the Solution.
entries.title: Thomassen: exponentially many 5-list-colourings of planar graphs

entries.abstract: A qualified actual-trial history theorem for convex MINLP, with full source definitions, pre-discovery exactness and fixed-fiber NLP polishing.
entries.title: Finite optimal-polish discovery for center-cut histories

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization around W. Duke and R. Schulze-Pillot, Representation of integers by positive ternary quadratic forms and equidistribution of lattice points on ellipsoids (Invent. Math. 99, 1990). q(x) = ½ xᵗAx for a symmetric integer 3 × 3 matrix A with q > 0 on ℚ³ \ {0}, h ∈ ℚ³, r(q, h, n) = #{x ∈ h + ℤ³ : q(x) = n} and, for F ⊆ ℝ³, r(q, F, h, n) = #{x ∈ h + ℤ³ : q(x) = n, x/√n ∈ F}. Unconditional results: card_divisors_le_rpow (d(n) ≤ C_ε n^ε); repCount_le (r(q, h, n) ≤ C_ε n^{1/2+ε} for n ≥ 1); average_le (the same bound for every nonnegatively weighted average of such counts, which includes r(spn_N q, h, n): this is the upper half of Lemma 5(ii)). Conditional results: thm3_ii (Theorem 3(ii), r(q, F, h, n) = R(n) μ(F) + O(n^{1/2 − 1/175 + ε}) for n ≥ 1 in a set S) and spn_upper (R(n) ≤ C_ε n^{1/2+ε}) are proved under two hypotheses that are NOT proved here: hThm1, the estimate of Theorem 1 of the paper (|r(q, F, h, n) − r(q, h, n) μ(F)| ≤ C (n^{−1/175} r(q, h, n) + n^{1/2−1/175+ε}) on S), and hThm3i, the estimate of Theorem 3(i) (|r(q, h, n) − R(n)| ≤ C n^{1/2−1/28+ε} on S); R stands for r(spn_N q, h, n), μF ∈ [0, 1] for μ(F), and S for the restricted set of n. The lower bound n^{1/2−ε} ≪ r(spn_N q, h, n) of Lemma 5(ii) (Siegel's ineffective bound) is not formalized.
entries.title: Duke–Schulze-Pillot: the upper bound of Lemma 5(ii) and a conditional Theorem 3(ii)

entries.abstract: The boxed finite conic-union continuous hull and compact lift. Finite bounds, explicit dependent residual dimensions and cone hypotheses are retained. Empty branches/index sets are allowed; this is not a general whole-GDP ideality theorem.
entries.title: Bounded finite conic-union hulls

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of the main results of Jacob Fox and László Miklós Lovász, A tight bound for Green's arithmetic triangle removal lemma in vector spaces (arXiv:1606.01230): the arithmetic triangle removal lemma in F_p^n with a polynomial bound (Theorem 1), the Kleinberg–Sawin–Speyer bound on multicolored sum-free families (Theorem 2), the count of triangles spanned by vertex-disjoint triangles (Theorem 3), and the tightness of the exponent in Theorem 1 (the second part of Theorem 1).
entries.title: A tight bound for Green's arithmetic triangle removal lemma in vector spaces

entries.abstract: Finite quantitative sparse-kernel and necessary expected-row bounds for independently subsampled binary Walsh matrices, with uniform asymptotic and recovery/RIP consequences.
entries.title: Sparse kernels and necessary sampling for binary Walsh matrices

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of two results on strictly 3-bicolored Steiner triple systems. For every positive triple of class sizes a,b,c, existence is equivalent to n=a+b+c being 1 or 3 modulo 6, the identity a²+b²+c²-ab-ac-bc=n, and the exclusion of two classes of size 2. For every sufficiently large admissible profile, the number of AAC blocks is characterized exactly by two explicit arithmetic tests. The first result settles the class-size conjecture posed by Colbourn, Dinitz and Rosa in 1999; the second applies the typed absorption theorems of Triangle decompositions III. Both statements are compared in one shared development.
entries.title: The Colbourn–Dinitz–Rosa conjecture and the exact block-type spectrum

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of D. Gale, A theorem on flows in networks (Pacific J. Math. 7, 1957) and of Hoffman's circulation theorem (A. J. Hoffman, 1960, in the form of A. Schrijver, A Course in Combinatorial Optimization, Theorems 4.6 and 4.7). A network is a finite node type N with capacities c : N → N → ℝ, c ≥ 0 (finite capacities only); a flow is f : N → N → ℝ with f x y + f y x = 0 and f ≤ c; a demand d : N → ℝ is feasible if some flow has net inflow ∑_y f y x ≥ d x at every node. feasibility: d is feasible if and only if d(Sᶜ) ≤ c(S, Sᶜ) for every S ⊆ N (Gale's Feasibility Theorem). feasibility_int: the same for integer c and d with an integer flow (Gale's remark). feasibility_second: Gale's second formulation (for every set Y of nodes of positive demand, some flow meets the demand at all nodes of nonpositive demand and the aggregate demand of Y). gale_ryser_unsorted, gale_ryser: for a : Fin m → ℕ and b : Fin n → ℕ, a 0-1 matrix with row sums at most a i and column sums b j exists if and only if ∑_{j∈Y} b j ≤ ∑_i min(a i, |Y|) for all column sets Y, equivalently, for b nonincreasing, ∑_{j<k} b j ≤ ∑_{j<k} #{i | j < a i} for all k ≤ n (Gale's Problem I, §3). gale_ryser_exact: if moreover ∑ a = ∑ b, the row sums can be made exactly a (the Gale–Ryser theorem). hoffman, hoffman_int: on a finite directed multigraph (arc type A, tail and head maps src, tgt : A → V) with bounds d ≤ c on the arcs (real, respectively integer), there is a circulation f (real, respectively integer) with d ≤ f ≤ c if and only if d(δ^in(U)) ≤ c(δ^out(U)) for every U ⊆ V. Eight statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: Gale's feasibility theorem, the Gale–Ryser theorem and Hoffman's circulation theorem

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.1 of Burgin, Fragkos, Kruzel, Lacey and Stokolosa (arXiv:2610.12831). For k ≥ 2 there are M_k ≤ exp(7 k log k) and P_k ≤ exp exp(25 k² log k), and an absolute constant C₁, such that for every prime p ≥ P_k there are C, c > 0 with the following property. Every A ⊆ F_p^n with n > exp^{(K)}(1) and density at least C / (log^{(K)} n)^c, where K = k^{C₁ k}, contains a restricted polynomial progression x, x + P_1(y), …, x + P_{k-1}(y), with P_j(y) = (y_1^j, …, y_n^j) and y ∈ {0, 2, 3, …, M_k}^n \ {0}. Moreover, the k points of any such progression are pairwise distinct. The formalization also proves the two theorems that the paper cites from the literature and does not prove. The first is the inverse theorem of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer for noise stability under distributions with no abelian embedding (Theorem 1.4 of the paper, which is Theorem 1 of their "On approximability of satisfiable k-CSPs: VII"), in full generality. The second is Dimitrov's theorem on the Schinzel–Zassenhaus conjecture (Theorem 5.11 of the paper). Only Lean's standard axioms are used.
entries.title: Reasonable bounds for restricted polynomial progressions in F_p^n

entries.abstract: The Johnson graph J(n, k) has the k-subsets of an n-set as vertices, two of them adjacent when they share k - 1 elements; an independent set is a constant-weight binary code of length n, weight k and minimum distance 4. This Lean 4 formalization proves Johnson's 1962 bound α(J(n, k)) ≤ johnsonBound n 4 k, where johnsonBound is the recursive bound A(n, d, w) ≤ ⌊n/w · A(n - 1, d, w - 1)⌋, as stated in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Erdős Problem 835), where it is a solved statement left without proof. The proof is by recursion on (n, k): double counting the pairs (point, member) and shortening the members through a point. No new mathematics is claimed.
entries.title: The Johnson bound for the independence number of the Johnson graph

entries.abstract: On the real square-summable states of the infinite centered octagonal cut-and-project vertex graph, take the graph Laplacian with edge weight 1/16, onsite potential V(x)=1+|p(x)|² and natural domain D(V). Add t times the coordinate projection onto the eight neighbors of the origin. At t*=17/16+√2 the two alternating ring modes meet at E*=13/4+√2. The full eigenspace at E* has real dimension exactly two. Every solution of the eigenvector equation is its amplitude at the lift (1,0,0,0) times the first compact state plus its amplitude at (1,1,0,0) times the second. No support restriction is assumed. Locality, symmetry and a strictly positive exterior energy force the exterior part to vanish; the complete central kernel supplies the two ring patterns.
entries.title: Spectral Geometry — exact multiplicity of a compact crossing on an infinite octagonal graph

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a weaker, fixed-density form of Theorem 2.1 of P. Keevash, Counting designs (J. Eur. Math. Soc. 20, 2018). density G is |E(G)| / C(n, 2); IsTypical G c h says that every nonempty set S of at most h vertices has (1 ± |S| c) d(G)^|S| n common neighbours; Tridivisible G says that every degree is even and 3 divides |E(G)|; IsTriangleDecomposition G D says that D is a family of triangles of G and every edge lies in exactly one of them. typical_triangle_decomposition: there is h such that for every d0 > 0 there are c0 > 0 and n0 such that every (c0, h)-typical tridivisible graph on n ≥ n0 vertices with density at least d0 has a triangle decomposition. This is weaker than the article in two ways: the density is bounded below by a fixed constant (the article allows d(G) > n^(-10^-7) with c < c0 d(G)^(10^6)), and the typicality is (c, h)-typicality for an absolute, not explicit, h (the article assumes c-typicality, which concerns only degrees and pairs). One statement.
entries.title: Triangle decompositions of typical graphs of fixed density (Keevash, Counting designs, Theorem 2.1, weaker form)

entries.abstract: Motivated by Alpöge's generic-degree-three counterexample to JC(3), we formalize the collision geometry of complex three-dimensional Keller maps of that degree. Using classical Keller–Galois rigidity, we identify the residual generic collision factor with the normal closure of the induced function-field extension, whose Galois group is S3. The decomposition separates the diagonal and proves nonvanishing of the collision obstruction.
entries.title: Generic Degree Three in JC(3): Collision Geometry and Galois Group S3

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of the principal results of the paper Representation embeddings and the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture. Over an algebraically closed field, every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra admits a faithful representation embedding of a colimit-closed category of Kronecker modules that preserves infinite dimensions (Theorem A). Hence, for every infinite cardinal κ, it has 2^κ pairwise non-isomorphic indecomposable modules of dimension κ whose endomorphism rings are local with residue field k and whose radicals satisfy (rad End M)^n = 0 for one n ≤ max(30, 4 dim A) independent of κ; for κ ≥ |k| this is the largest possible number (Corollary 1.1, in full). Weaker parts of the corollary are also compared: modules of every infinite dimension, the endomorphism control without the count and the bound, and the count without the bound. The cited inputs are proved in the library: Bongartz's Theorem 6 and Göbel and Simson's rigid families over infinite fields.
entries.title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof that, over a field of characteristic zero, the Dixmier conjecture in dimension n implies the Jacobian conjecture in dimension n (Bass, Connell and Wright, 1982), and so, with an explicit counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture padded to every dimension n >= 3 and proved here, that the Dixmier conjecture is false in every dimension n >= 3. The four statements and their definitions are Formal Conjectures' (DixmierConjecture.lean, arXiv math/0608009), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statements. The proof builds the polynomial representation of the Weyl algebra, shows it faithful in characteristic zero, and uses the classical Weyl-algebra lift described by Bass, Connell and Wright (1982, p. 297), who credit Vaserstein and Kac.
entries.title: The Dixmier conjecture implies the Jacobian conjecture, and is false in dimension 3 and above

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of both maximum-modulus counting questions of Hayman–Lingham Problem 2.16 (Erdős Problem 1117). For an entire function f and a radius r, let ν(f, r) be the number of points on the circle |z| = r where |f| attains its maximum on that circle. The registered theorem proves two things: some non-monomial entire function has ν(f, r) unbounded along radii tending to infinity; and for every non-monomial entire function there is one finite bound B with ν(f, r) ≤ B along a cofinal set of radii, so the counts never tend to infinity. The first part follows Pardo-Simón and Sixsmith's finite-order construction and proves the approximation step of Rempe-Gillen that it uses; the second follows Li's cofinal-bound argument. The theorem depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Maximum-modulus points of entire functions (Erdős Problem 1117), in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of exponential separation for analytic iterated function systems on the real line. Strong exponential separation holds on an open and dense subset in the C2 topology and follows from an explicit criterion involving dual projections. The development characterises conjugacy to self-similar systems and proves dimension consequences, including a drop in the L^q dimensions of the natural measure of a concrete three-map example, together with the cited results of Rapaport and Bowen.
entries.title: Exponential separation of analytic self-conformal sets on the real line: Lean formalisation

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem of Chudnovsky, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas: a finite graph is perfect if and only if it is Berge. A graph is perfect if every induced subgraph has chromatic number equal to its clique number. It is Berge if neither the graph nor its complement contains an induced cycle of odd length at least five. The proof follows the paper of Chudnovsky, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas (Annals of Mathematics, 2006). It formalizes the decomposition theorem for Berge graphs (Theorem 1.3 of the paper) through the numbered results of Sections 2 to 24. It also proves the earlier results that the paper cites, among them Lovász's weak perfect graph theorem, the results of Cornuéjols and Cunningham on 2-joins, of Chvátal and Sbihi on homogeneous pairs, of Chvátal on star cutsets, and of Roussel and Rubio. The statement in Challenge.lean uses only Mathlib's definitions of induced subgraphs, chromatic number, clique number, cycle graphs and induced containment.
entries.title: The Strong Perfect Graph Theorem

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. Write ||x|| = |x - round x| for the distance from a real number to the nearest integer, and let rho be the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 and the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944). Convergence of sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 for a Pisot number theta is elementary, and Pisot (1938) proved the converse; neither gives the value. (1) For every real rho with rho^3 = rho + 1, sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho (as a HasSum). (2) The tsum form of (1).
